Subject: Weekly MAP — performance checkpoint: latency & throughput (MedSync)

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks for joining the MAP cadence — quick weekly checkpoint notes attached and a short recap of the perf benchmarking we ran this morning against the evaluation prompts you shared. Goal for today: confirm whether results meet the latency SLOs in the MAP and agree next tuning steps + owners so we can keep to the proposed close timeline.

High level:
- Test harness: 8k-token context snapshots, 1k-token responses where applicable (representative of production flows).
- Model variant: open-llm-2.2-16b (quantized int8x4) served on p4d-equivalent nodes in our Dedicated pool.
- Traffic shape: mix of chat and single-call generation; we ran 500 warm-up requests then sampled 2,000 measurement calls.

I attached the MAP tracker and raw logs for reference (medsync_map_v2.xlsx, latency_logs_20260601.tar.gz).

Proposed agenda for next internal checkpoint:
- Review p50/p95 numbers (we include them below)
- Decide whether to move to increased batching / lower-precision quant on the model in A/B
- Confirm owners for the three immediate action items

Please see Priyom's detailed benchmark email below for exact numbers.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Alex —

Appreciate the summary and the files. Quick notes from our side after a skim:
- The p95 numbers will be the gating factor for our care workflows — anything consistently over 700ms for inference end-to-end will require us to revert to a pull model.
- We need a breakdown by route: triage (short prompts), summary (longer context), and batch embeddings (for nightly jobs). Can you confirm whether the 2,000 measurement calls include a route-level split?
- Also can Priyom attach the raw histogram and a short note on whether KV-cache warm times were included in the p95?

If we can get those details today that would help us decide on the next MAP milestone.

—Elena
VP Platform, MedSync Health

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medsynchealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP — performance checkpoint: latency & throughput (MedSync)

Hi all — attaching the summarized numbers and a couple of notes from the run this morning. See also attached tiny histogram snippets inside the latency_logs_20260601.tar.gz (top-level files: p50_p95_histograms.txt).

Benchmark summary (2,000 measurement calls after 500 warm-ups) — route split: triage=800, summary=900, embeddings=300. All numbers are end-to-end inference latency measured at the service edge (includes network hop to Dedicated nodes in us-west-2 but excludes post-processing on client).

Triage (short prompts, median response length ~80 tokens):
- p50: 78 ms
- p95: 210 ms
- peak concurrency tested: 48 rps sustained for 60s

Summary (longer context, median response length ~850 tokens):
- p50: 420 ms
- p95: 860 ms
- note: p95 here includes first-request KV-cache miss cases; warm-cache p95 drops to ~620 ms

Embeddings (batch size 128 tokens per item in batch):
- throughput: 2,300 vectors/sec (on single node)
- p95 (single item latency): 140 ms

Cost / config notes:
- Run used quantized int8x4 — gave ~1.9x cost improvement vs fp16 baseline with ~5% quality delta on eval samples (see MAP eval sheet).
- We observed ~10–12% tail increase when concurrency > 64 due to queueing; batching for summaries helps but increases p50 for single calls slightly.

Answers to Elena's questions:
- Yes, the 2,000 calls were split as above across routes.
- The reported summary p95 includes KV-cache miss cases; warm-cache numbers included above for clarity. The histograms in the logs show the warm vs cold distribution.

Recommended short-term tunings (win / cost tradeoffs):
1) Warm-cache priming for summary-heavy endpoints — schedule a lightweight priming job 30s before expected peak windows (owner: laura_bennett). Expected p95 improvement: ~15–25% on summary route.
2) Route-aware batching: enable small batching window (10–20ms) for summaries when concurrency > 30 to improve throughput without materially increasing average latency for triage. (owner: priyom_das).
3) A/B test a lower-precision quant variant (int4 experimental) on a canary subset (~5% traffic) to measure quality delta in the MAP eval harness before full rollout (owner: alex_martinez / MedSync).

Action items captured below. I can push the updated histograms and raw CSVs to the Drive link if you want the per-request CSV.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Perf Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -07:00

Adding tactical runbook items and owners below. I will own the priming job and the short batching window experiment.

Runbook / Immediate next steps (ETA in business days):
- LAUNCH: Cache priming lambda (once per hour, adjustable) — owner: laura_bennett — ETA: 1 day (dev + smoke).
- EXPERIMENT: Route-aware batching 10ms window on summary route behind runtime toggle — owner: priyom_das — ETA: 2 days (test + perf regression).
- A/B: int4 canary (5% traffic) with automated eval checks against MAP prompt set — owner: alex_martinez + MedSync eng lead (Tom) — ETA: 3 days to spin canary, 7 days to collect quality metrics.
- DECISION: If warm-cache + batching yields summary p95 <=700ms on warm requests and cold <=800ms, move to expanded canary and finalize MAP milestone 3.

I'll push the cache priming script to the repo and link in the Drive doc. Priyom — please push the per-request CSVs so I can validate warm vs cold split quickly.

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
